blogs.title: The Pre-Op Cath Trap: Why HIT Can Strike Before Day 5 After Cardiac Surgery
blogs.description: This post dissects the critical teaching point that the 'classic' Day 5–10 window for post-cardiac surgery HIT can be significantly shortened by recent pre-operative heparin exposure. We will analyze how a seemingly minor dose of unfractionated heparin during a diagnostic catheterization one week prior primed this patient's immune system, leading to an accelerated and devastating onset of thrombocytopenia immediately after bypass. Clinicians will learn to expand their differential for early post-op platelet drops beyond hemodilution and consumption when recent heparin exposure exists.

blogs.title: Beyond Heparin-Dependence: Recognizing the Serological Signature of Autoimmune HIT
blogs.description: Focusing on the laboratory nuances, this article explains the distinction between classic HIT and the more severe Autoimmune HIT (aHIT). We will break down the atypical Serotonin Release Assay (SRA) profile seen in this case: strong platelet activation even in the *absence* of heparin (heparin-independent activation) and, uniquely, partial resistance to Fc receptor blockade. This post aims to prevent clinicians from dismissing an 'indeterminate' functional assay when the clinical picture suggests a hypercoagulable storm, emphasizing that aHIT antibodies behave differently than standard PF4/heparin complexes.

blogs.title: When Argatroban Isn't Enough: Escalating Therapy in Refractory Autoimmune HIT
blogs.description: This management-focused post explores the therapeutic challenges of severe aHIT, where standard care (direct thrombin inhibitors like argatroban and IVIG) may fail to halt the hypercoagulable state. We will discuss the clinical markers of treatment failure in this case—including falling fibrinogen, rising D-dimers, and new schistocytes—and rationale for switching to high-dose fondaparinux supplemented with antithrombin concentrate. It serves as a guide for recognizing 'breakthrough' thrombosis in treated HIT and considering alternative anticoagulant mechanisms.

blogs.title: Stroke in the Setting of Thrombocytopenia: Navigating the Anticoagulation Paradox
blogs.description: Addressing the terrifying scenario of a new ischemic stroke occurring while platelet counts plummet to <20k/µL, this post discusses risk stratification and decision-making in aHIT. Unlike typical ITP or drug-induced thrombocytopenia where bleeding is the primary fear, aHIT presents a paradoxical state of extreme clotting risk despite severe thrombocytopenia. We will review why withholding anticoagulation is dangerous in this specific entity and how to balance the risks of hemorrhagic transformation against life-threatening propagating thrombosis.

blogs.title: The Consumptive Coagulopathy Mimic: Differentiating Severe aHIT from TTP and DIC
blogs.description: With features like schistocytes, severe thrombocytopenia, and organ injury (stroke), severe aHIT can masquerade as Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP) or Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC). This educational piece uses the case details—specifically the preserved haptoglobin initially, the specific timing relative to heparin, and the unique coagulation profile—to teach clinicians how to distinguish these entities. Understanding these differences is vital, as treatments like plasma exchange (for TTP) or cryoprecipitate (for DIC) do not address the underlying antibody-driven pathology of aHIT.
